basic_identification.name: AI model ecosystems for artists
basic_identification.originator: Stability AI (Emad Mostaque, Stable Diffusion 2022). Midjourney (David Holz, 2022). OpenAI (DALL-E, 2021). RunwayML (Cristobal Valenzuela, Alejandro Matamala, 2018). ComfyUI (comfyanonymous, 2023). Community: Civitai for model sharing, Hugging Face for open models. LoRA technique from Microsoft Research.
basic_identification.year: 2022 (mass adoption breakout with Stable Diffusion and Midjourney)
basic_identification.geography: Global. Stability AI (London), Midjourney (San Francisco), OpenAI (San Francisco), RunwayML (New York). Open-source community is globally distributed. Strong adoption in US, Europe, East Asia, South America.

core_ideas.core_claim: Generative AI models enable artists to create images, video, audio, and 3D content through natural language prompts and visual controls, fundamentally expanding who can create and how. The ecosystem spans closed commercial platforms (Midjourney, DALL-E) to fully open-source systems (Stable Diffusion + ComfyUI) offering maximum customization and control.
core_ideas.medium_specificity: Entirely digitally native. These tools create new forms of computational image-making where the model's latent space becomes a creative medium. The specificity is in the prompt-to-image translation, the ability to traverse latent spaces, fine-tune models on specific aesthetics (LoRA), and build complex generation pipelines (ComfyUI workflows). This is not simulation of traditional media but a new mode of image production.
core_ideas.relation_to_attention_economy: Deeply entangled. Social media virality drives adoption (Midjourney images dominate visual social media). The ease of generation creates an attention surplus: more images produced than can receive meaningful attention. Platform design (Midjourney's Discord gallery, Civitai trending models) optimizes for engagement. The speed of generation rewards prolific posting over contemplative practice. However, the open-source ecosystem (Stable Diffusion, ComfyUI) enables private, non-performative use that escapes attention logic.
core_ideas.relation_to_intention: Dual nature. The tools can serve intention (artists using AI as a medium for deliberate creative practice) or attention (mass generation for social media engagement, content farm production). The ecosystem does not inherently favor either. Midjourney's curation of aesthetic quality suggests some intention-alignment, while the ease of generation and social sharing mechanics pull toward attention capture. The artist's choice of tool and practice determines alignment.

market_economics.revenue_model: Midjourney: subscription ($10-60/month). DALL-E: credit-based via ChatGPT Plus ($20/month). RunwayML: subscription with generation credits. Stable Diffusion: free (open-source), but GPU costs for local running or cloud compute fees. ComfyUI: 100% free and open-source. Civitai: freemium model marketplace. The open-source ecosystem enables zero-cost entry with hardware investment only.
market_economics.market_position: Tool layer with emerging platform characteristics. Midjourney operates as a walled garden. Stable Diffusion + ComfyUI is open infrastructure. RunwayML bridges creative tools and AI. The market is bifurcating between convenience (closed platforms) and control (open-source).
market_economics.price_range: Tool costs: $0 (open-source) to $720/year (Midjourney Pro). Art created with AI tools has no established price range; some AI-assisted artists sell for thousands at galleries while the vast majority of AI-generated images have zero market value. The 2024 Sotheby's sale of AI art by Refik Anadol at $6.2M represents the high end.
market_economics.volume_trend_2024_2026: Rapidly growing. Generative AI adoption among creative professionals rose from 33% (2023) to 71% (2024). The global AI in art market was $3.2B in 2024, projected to reach $40.4B by 2033. Video generation (Sora, Runway Gen-3, Kling) is the current growth frontier. However, individual platform trajectories vary: Stability AI has faced financial difficulties while Midjourney and open-source alternatives thrive.
market_economics.collector_demographics: Largely undefined for AI-generated art as such. Traditional collectors remain skeptical. Crypto-native collectors have embraced some AI art (Refik Anadol). The mass of AI-generated images has no collector base. A small but growing segment of art world collectors accept AI as a medium when used by established artists. [uncertain]
market_economics.sustainability: Uncertain. Closed platforms depend on subscription revenue and massive compute costs. Midjourney appears profitable. Stability AI has struggled financially despite pioneering the open model approach. Open-source models depend on community maintenance and hardware accessibility. The ecosystem's sustainability is tied to ongoing GPU cost reduction, model efficiency improvements, and whether artistic AI use can differentiate itself from commercial content generation. [uncertain]

practice_aesthetics.toolchain: Stable Diffusion (model) + ComfyUI (workflow) + ControlNet (spatial control) + LoRA (style fine-tuning) + IPAdapter (image guidance) is the power-user stack. Midjourney via Discord. DALL-E via ChatGPT. RunwayML for video. Civitai and Hugging Face for model discovery. Local deployment requires NVIDIA GPUs (8GB+ VRAM minimum, 24GB recommended). Cloud alternatives: ThinkDiffusion, Replicate, fal.ai.
practice_aesthetics.relation_to_AI: This IS the AI art tool layer. The central tension is between AI as tool (artist retains creative agency, uses AI as one element in a broader practice) and AI as autonomous creator (text prompt in, finished image out). The ecosystem increasingly supports the tool model: ControlNet for precise spatial control, LoRA for stylistic specificity, ComfyUI for complex multi-step workflows. However, the dominant use case remains prompt-to-image generation where AI makes most creative decisions.
practice_aesthetics.liveness: Primarily static artifact generation, but evolving toward: real-time generation (Stable Diffusion turbo models), interactive installations (camera-to-generation pipelines), live performance (real-time style transfer), and video generation. ComfyUI workflows can be real-time and interactive. The ecosystem is moving from batch artifact production to real-time generative systems.
practice_aesthetics.aesthetic_vocabulary: Rapidly developing but contested. Prompt engineering, latent space, diffusion, denoising, CFG scale, LoRA, checkpoint, safetensors, ControlNet, inpainting, outpainting, img2img, txt2img, seed, sampler, negative prompt. Critical vocabulary is less developed: 'AI slop' (pejorative for generic AI output), 'AI art' (contested term), 'co-creation,' 'human-AI collaboration.' The field lacks adequate critical language to distinguish between superficially similar AI outputs with vastly different artistic intention and process.
practice_aesthetics.tendency_axis_position: Bifurcated. Open-source ecosystem (Stable Diffusion, ComfyUI): strongly open, commons-oriented, infrastructure-focused. Closed platforms (Midjourney, DALL-E): enclosed, capture-oriented, spectacle-focused. The field as a whole trends toward individual production (prompt-to-image) rather than collective practice. The open-source side contributes significantly to commons; the closed side encloses.

infrastructure_governance.openness: Spectrum. Stable Diffusion: open-source (various licenses, SDXL is open). ComfyUI: GPL. Flux models: open weights. LoRA/fine-tuning techniques: openly published. Midjourney: fully closed, no local running. DALL-E: closed API only. RunwayML: proprietary with API access. The open-source side is genuinely open; the commercial side is genuinely closed. This bifurcation is the ecosystem's defining structural feature.
infrastructure_governance.governance_model: Stability AI: corporate (venture-backed, troubled governance, CEO departures). Midjourney: small team, founder-led, opaque decision-making. OpenAI: corporate with nonprofit origins (much-debated governance). ComfyUI: community-driven, founder-led open-source project. The governance landscape is fragmented with no industry coordination on standards, ethics, or interoperability.
infrastructure_governance.data_sovereignty: Critical weakness. Most models were trained on data scraped from the internet without artist consent (LAION-5B dataset). Artists have limited ability to remove their work from trained models. Closed platforms retain generated outputs on their servers. Open-source tools enable local generation with no data leaving the user's machine. The training data consent crisis is the ecosystem's most significant ethical challenge.
infrastructure_governance.interoperability: Growing within the open ecosystem. ComfyUI nodes can integrate models from different sources. Safetensors format is a shared model distribution standard. LoRAs and ControlNet modules work across compatible models. However, Midjourney, DALL-E, and RunwayML are walled gardens with no cross-platform workflow. The open-source ecosystem is highly interoperable; the commercial ecosystem is fragmented.
infrastructure_governance.preservation_strategy: Open models and weights can be preserved as files. ComfyUI workflows are saved as JSON, enabling reproduction. Generated images are standard files. However, the rapid model evolution means specific outputs may be irreproducible as models are superseded. No systematic archival of AI art tools or outputs exists. Closed platform outputs are at-risk if platforms shut down.
infrastructure_governance.consent_architecture: The ecosystem's deepest structural failure. Most training datasets were compiled without creator consent. Spawning/HaveIBeenTrained provides opt-out infrastructure but adoption by AI companies is voluntary. Stability AI and Hugging Face agreed to honor Spawning's do-not-train registry. Midjourney and OpenAI's consent architecture is opaque. The EU AI Act and various lawsuits are forcing consent infrastructure development, but it remains inadequate.

field_position.relation_to_traditional_art_world: Contested integration. Major galleries and auction houses have exhibited and sold AI art (Refik Anadol at MoMA, Christie's AI art sales). Art fairs increasingly include AI-generated work. However, significant resistance from traditional artists and critics who question authorship, skill, and artistic merit. Photography's historical struggle for acceptance is often cited as a parallel. The 2023 Washtington Post-viral Colorado State Fair AI art controversy crystallized the debate.
field_position.what_it_enables: Visual creation accessible to non-artists (democratization or deskilling, depending on perspective). Rapid iteration and prototyping for professional artists. New aesthetic possibilities exploring latent spaces. Custom model training for specific styles or subjects. Complex multi-step generation pipelines (ComfyUI). Video and 3D content generation. AI-assisted art that combines human and machine creativity in novel ways.
field_position.what_it_lacks: Consent infrastructure for training data. Clear attribution models for AI-assisted work. Critical frameworks adequate to evaluate AI art beyond novelty or technical prowess. Tools for artists to understand what their models have learned and from whom. Mechanisms for compensating artists whose work contributed to model training. Preservation strategies for AI art practice documentation. The ability to trace specific outputs to training data influences.
field_position.who_is_excluded: Artists without GPU hardware or cloud compute budgets (for open-source). Artists in regions with restricted internet access. Artists whose consent was violated by training data scraping (they are involuntary participants, not excluded, but their agency is denied). Artists whose aesthetic vocabulary was homogenized by model biases. Non-English speakers face reduced prompt effectiveness. Blind and visually impaired artists are excluded from visual-generation tools. Communities whose visual culture is underrepresented in training data receive poor generation quality.
field_position.frontier_signal: Frontier across the board. Video generation (Sora, Runway Gen-3, Kling), 3D generation, real-time generation, multi-modal models, and custom model training are all active frontiers. The challenge is shifting from what AI can generate to what it should generate and how authorship, consent, and attribution should function. The technology is ahead of the ethical and institutional frameworks.

attention_intention.discovery_mechanism: Social media (Twitter/X, Reddit, YouTube tutorials), Discord communities, Civitai model marketplace trending lists, word of mouth, tech journalism, YouTube channels (Stability AI official, ComfyUI tutorials), conference presentations. Discovery is heavily social-media-driven.
attention_intention.attention_dependency: High for commercial platforms. Midjourney's growth was entirely social-media-driven (Discord virality). Stable Diffusion's adoption was driven by Reddit, Twitter, and YouTube coverage. If social media disappeared, the tools would persist but adoption would slow dramatically. The open-source ecosystem has more resilient discovery through GitHub, documentation, and community forums.
attention_intention.intention_alignment: Mixed. The tools can serve artistic intention (fine-tuned models for specific practices, ComfyUI workflows for controlled generation) or attention capture (mass generation for social media, content farming). The ecosystem's defaults favor ease and volume over deliberation and meaning. Artists who use these tools intentionally must actively resist the pull toward attention-optimized production.
attention_intention.commons_contribution: Bifurcated. Open-source ecosystem: massive commons contribution through shared models, workflows, tutorials, techniques. Civitai, Hugging Face, and ComfyUI communities exemplify open knowledge sharing. Closed platforms: minimal commons contribution, enclosed proprietary systems. The training data crisis undermines commons claims: open models built on unconsented data are extractive commons that take from artists without reciprocity.

provenance_temporality.provenance_type: Neither, primarily. Generated outputs typically have no provenance tracking. Some platforms embed C2PA metadata (Content Credentials) for AI-generated content detection, but this is provenance of origin (was this AI-made?) rather than provenance of ownership or meaning. The training data provenance (what data influenced this output?) is technically impossible to reconstruct from a generated image.
provenance_temporality.temporal_logic: Primarily anticipatory (what can we generate next?) and real-time (generation as live process). No deep-historical awareness. Model versions replace each other rapidly. The ecosystem is presentist, focused on the latest model capabilities rather than understanding or preserving its own short history.
provenance_temporality.absence_handling: Significant absences are structural but unacknowledged. Training data biases create systematic absences: visual cultures not represented in LAION-5B produce poor generation quality. The consent of artists whose work trained the models is absent. Documentation of artistic process (beyond final outputs) is largely absent. The ecosystem does not represent or address its own gaps.

coherence.coherence_vs_consensus: Neither coherence nor consensus. The field is in active, unresolved conflict. Is AI art real art? Is prompting creative authorship? Should training data require consent? Is open-source AI democratizing or enabling exploitation? These questions have no coherent shared framework, let alone consensus. Different communities (AI artists, traditional artists, ethicists, technologists, lawyers) operate with incompatible values.
coherence.contestability: High. Every aspect of the ecosystem is actively contested: authorship, consent, quality, value, legality, ethics. Ongoing lawsuits (Getty v. Stability AI, Andersen v. Stability AI et al.) are contesting fundamental legal questions. The USCO's guidance on AI copyrightability represents institutional contestation. Artists contest through tools (Glaze, Nightshade) and advocacy (Spawning). The ecosystem is defined by contestation.
coherence.forkability: High for open-source components. Stable Diffusion has been forked numerous times. ComfyUI is forkable. LoRAs and custom models are inherently forkable. Closed platforms (Midjourney, DALL-E) cannot be forked. The bifurcation between forkable and non-forkable mirrors the open/closed divide.

adai_comparison.what_adai_should_adopt: The open-source ecosystem's commons-first model building approach. ComfyUI's node-based workflow architecture as a model for composable, transparent processes. The community-driven model sharing and improvement culture. The recognition that tools shape practice and must be understood to map the field. The principle that infrastructure should be transparent and auditable.
adai_comparison.what_adai_should_refuse: The training data consent violation as a foundational practice. The attention-optimized production model that prioritizes volume over meaning. The presentist temporal logic that discards its own history. The aesthetic homogenization that results from shared model biases. The conflation of generation with creation. The enclosure of knowledge by closed platforms. The disregard for artist agency and livelihood.
adai_comparison.structural_tension: AI model ecosystems are the fastest-evolving layer of the digital art field, yet they are also the most ethically contested and the least historically self-aware. A(DAI) must track this layer rigorously (it is reshaping practice, markets, and discourse simultaneously) while maintaining critical distance from its attention-optimized values. The tension is between the need to understand AI's impact on the field and the refusal to normalize consent violations and aesthetic homogenization as acceptable costs of innovation.

regulatory_legal.regulatory_exposure: Extremely high and rapidly evolving. EU AI Act classifies generative AI systems as requiring transparency disclosures. US copyright law (Thaler v. Perlmutter) denies copyright to purely AI-generated works. Multiple ongoing lawsuits contest training data legality (Getty v. Stability AI, Andersen v. Stability AI). California AB 2013 requires AI training data disclosure. UK copyright exception for text and data mining creates different rules. China requires registration of generative AI services. The regulatory landscape is fragmented and in flux.
regulatory_legal.ip_model: Deeply contested. Model weights: various open licenses (Apache 2.0, custom licenses). Generated outputs: no copyright protection for fully AI-generated works (US, as of 2025). Human-AI collaborative works: case-by-case determination of sufficient human authorship. Training data: claimed as fair use by AI companies, contested by artists and rights holders in court. LoRAs trained on specific artists' work raise unresolved IP questions.
regulatory_legal.opt_in_vs_opt_out: Predominantly opt-out, which is the core ethical failure. Training data was collected without consent. Artists must actively opt out (via Spawning, robots.txt, platform-specific mechanisms) rather than being asked to opt in. The EU AI Act and ongoing litigation may force a shift toward opt-in, but this has not occurred yet. Spawning's Source.Plus represents an emerging opt-in model for ethical training data.

ecosystem.platform_dependency: Varies dramatically. Midjourney: complete dependency on Midjourney Inc. and Discord. DALL-E: dependent on OpenAI. Stable Diffusion: distributed, no single dependency (models downloadable, multiple UIs). ComfyUI: open-source, no platform dependency. All GPU-dependent workflows depend on NVIDIA (market dominance in AI-capable GPUs). Cloud services create dependency on compute providers.
ecosystem.network_effects: Strong. Midjourney benefits from community gallery and shared prompt knowledge. Civitai's model marketplace has strong network effects (more models attract more users attract more model creators). ComfyUI's node ecosystem benefits from developer network effects. Training data itself represents a controversial network effect: more data creates better models creates more users creates more data. Open-source model sharing creates positive-sum network effects.
ecosystem.post_crash_trajectory: Growing rapidly, independent of NFT crash. The AI art tool ecosystem was nascent during the NFT boom (Stable Diffusion launched August 2022, after NFT peak). The trajectory is exponential adoption with ongoing ethical/legal reckoning. The market is splitting between professional creative tools (RunwayML for filmmakers) and consumer-accessible generation (Midjourney, DALL-E). The open-source ecosystem is the fastest-growing segment.
